TOPICS.title: Stair rise and run
TOPICS.summary: Rise and run are measured nosing to nosing and must be uniform within a flight. Private stairs (inside a dwelling unit, or exterior stairs serving one dwelling unit) allow a steeper stair than public stairs.
values: Private: rise 125–200 mm, run 255–355 mm
Public: rise 125–180 mm, run ≥ 280 mm
Max vertical rise of one flight: 3.7 m (then a landing)
TOPICS.on: OBC 2024 adopted the NBC 2020 values — the old OBC 2012 minimum private run of 210 mm no longer applies.
TOPICS.tags: stairs step riser tread going nosing landing flight

TOPICS.title: Stair width and headroom
TOPICS.summary: Minimum clear width between wall faces or guards, and minimum clear headroom measured vertically from the stair nosing line.
values: Stairs serving a single dwelling unit: width ≥ 860 mm
Other residential exit and public stairs: width ≥ 900 mm
Headroom: typically 1950 mm in dwelling units, 2050 mm elsewhere
TOPICS.tags: stair width headroom clearance

TOPICS.title: Handrails
TOPICS.summary: Where handrails are required, how many sides, their height, graspability and extensions at the top and bottom of a flight.
values: Height: 865–965 mm measured above the nosing line
Wider stairs need handrails on both sides — check the width threshold in 9.8.7.1
TOPICS.tags: handrail rail grab stairs ramp

TOPICS.title: Guards (railings)
TOPICS.summary: Guards are required where the difference in level is more than 600 mm. Height depends on location; openings must stop a small sphere passing through, and guards in dwellings must not be easily climbable.
values: Required where drop > 600 mm
Height ≥ 900 mm inside a dwelling unit (and some exterior guards ≤ 1.8 m above grade)
Height ≥ 1070 mm elsewhere
Openings must not let a 100 mm sphere pass
TOPICS.tags: guard railing balcony deck baluster fall

TOPICS.title: Ramps
TOPICS.summary: Slope, width, landings and handrails for ramps. Barrier-free ramps in Section 3.8 are stricter than ordinary ramps.
values: Barrier-free ramp slope: not steeper than 1 in 12
Level landings at the top, bottom, at intervals of not more than 9 m and where the ramp turns
Handrails on both sides, 865–965 mm high
A walk steeper than 1 in 20 in a barrier-free path is a ramp
TOPICS.tags: ramp slope accessible wheelchair
TOPICS.on: Ontario's barrier-free ramp article is 3.8.3.4; landings must be at least 1 670 mm long. Use the Accessible ramp calculator to size runs and landings.
TOPICS.bc: Barrier-free ramps are in Article 3.8.3.5. Use the Accessible ramp calculator to size runs and landings.

TOPICS.title: Bedroom egress windows
TOPICS.summary: Each bedroom (or a combined bedroom) in a dwelling unit without a sprinkler system needs a window or door that opens to the outside for escape.
values: Unobstructed opening ≥ 0.35 m²
No opening dimension less than 380 mm
TOPICS.tags: egress window bedroom escape basement

TOPICS.title: Smoke alarms
TOPICS.summary: Where smoke alarms go in dwelling units, how they are powered and interconnected.
values: Required on every storey and in (or near) sleeping rooms — check exact locations
Interconnected within a dwelling unit
TOPICS.tags: smoke alarm detector fire safety

TOPICS.title: Spatial separation & limiting distance
TOPICS.summary: Limits the area of unprotected openings (windows, doors) in an exposing building face based on its limiting distance to the property line — the closer you are, the fewer windows you can have and the more fire-resistance the wall needs.
TOPICS.tags: limiting distance unprotected openings windows property line fire

TOPICS.title: Fire separations between suites
TOPICS.summary: Fire separations and fire-resistance ratings required between dwelling units, and between dwelling units and other occupancies or common areas.
TOPICS.tags: fire separation rating suite party wall

TOPICS.title: Exits & travel distance (Part 3)
TOPICS.summary: How many exits a floor area needs, maximum travel distance to an exit, and exit widths based on occupant load.
TOPICS.tags: exit travel distance egress occupant load corridor

TOPICS.title: Ceiling heights & room sizes
TOPICS.summary: Minimum ceiling heights and minimum room areas for living spaces, bedrooms, kitchens and bathrooms in dwelling units are set out in tables in Section 9.5.
TOPICS.tags: ceiling height room size area bedroom minimum

TOPICS.title: Natural light & ventilation
TOPICS.summary: Minimum glazed area for natural light in rooms, and mechanical / natural ventilation requirements for houses.
TOPICS.tags: window glazing daylight natural light ventilation

TOPICS.title: Energy efficiency
TOPICS.ref: Part 9 houses: Section 9.36 · larger buildings: referenced energy codes
TOPICS.refOn: Part 9 houses: SB-12 (Supplementary Standard) via Section 12.2 · larger buildings: SB-10
TOPICS.summary: Energy performance requirements for the building envelope, HVAC and hot water, via prescriptive, trade-off or performance paths.
TOPICS.bc: BC adds the Energy Step Code (performance tiers local governments can require) and the Zero Carbon Step Code for greenhouse-gas emissions.
TOPICS.on: Ontario Part 9 housing uses Supplementary Standard SB-12; larger buildings use SB-10.
TOPICS.tags: energy insulation envelope step code sb-12 sb-10 9.36 carbon

TOPICS.title: Barrier-free / accessible design
TOPICS.summary: Where barrier-free paths of travel, entrances, washrooms, parking and suites are required, and the design requirements for each. For entrances, doors, ramps, washrooms, adaptable units and the key dimensions, open the accessibility finder.
TOPICS.bc: BCBC 2024 adds adaptable dwelling unit requirements (Subsection 3.8.5) for some multi-unit residential buildings.
TOPICS.on: Ontario Section 3.8 barrier-free design — houses are generally exempt; check the application clauses.
TOPICS.tags: accessible barrier-free wheelchair adaptable universal design washroom

TOPICS.title: Occupancy classification
TOPICS.summary: Classifies buildings by major occupancy — Group A (assembly), B (care / detention), C (residential), D (business), E (mercantile), F (industrial) — which drives most other requirements.
TOPICS.tags: occupancy classification group a b c d e f assembly residential

TOPICS.title: Part 3 or Part 9?
TOPICS.summary: Part 9 (Housing and Small Buildings) covers smaller residential, business, mercantile and low / medium-hazard industrial buildings; everything else is Part 3.
values: Part 9: typically ≤ 3 storeys in building height and ≤ 600 m² building area (for the listed occupancies)
TOPICS.tags: part 9 part 3 small buildings housing application

TOPICS.title: Building size & construction type
TOPICS.summary: Maximum building height and area by occupancy and sprinklering, and whether construction must be combustible, noncombustible or encapsulated mass timber.
TOPICS.tags: building height area storeys combustible noncombustible mass timber

TOPICS.title: Climatic & seismic data
TOPICS.ref: Division B, Appendix C (climatic and seismic information)
TOPICS.summary: Design snow, wind, rain, temperature and seismic values by location — you need these for structure and envelope design.
TOPICS.tags: snow load wind load climate seismic design data location

bc.name: BC Building Code 2024
bc.note: In force since March 8, 2024. It does not apply in the City of Vancouver, which has its own Vancouver Building By-law (VBBL) — check the VBBL for Vancouver sites.

on.name: Ontario Building Code 2024 (O. Reg. 163/24)
on.note: In force since January 1, 2025, and harmonized more closely with the National Building Code 2020. Older OBC 2012 values you find online may be out of date.

bc.name: BC Building Code 2024 — Section 3.8 Accessibility
bc.note: Based on NBC 2020, with BC additions: power-operated doors, elevators in larger low-rise buildings, adult changing spaces, and adaptable dwelling units from March 10, 2025. Not used in the City of Vancouver, which has its own by-law (VBBL).

links.label: Accessibility requirements in the BC Building Code — gov.bc.ca
Adaptable Dwelling Unit Illustrative Design Guide (PDF) — gov.bc.ca

on.name: Ontario Building Code 2024 — Section 3.8 Barrier-Free Design
on.note: Ontario keeps its own barrier-free Section 3.8, so several numbers differ from BC and the National Building Code. Accessible parking and some public spaces are also governed by the AODA standards.

links.label: Accessibility in Ontario's Building Code — ontario.ca

TOPICS.title: Which buildings need accessible design
TOPICS.summary: Section 3.8 applies to most new buildings. Small residential buildings are the main exception, so read the application article before you design.
TOPICS.tags: application exemption exempt house duplex townhouse row house scope

values: Exempt: detached and semi-detached houses, houses with a secondary suite, duplexes, triplexes, townhouses and row houses
Some high-hazard industrial buildings are also exempt
bc.note: Several dimensions grew from BCBC 2018 to 2024. Details and guides based on the 2018 code may be out of date.

values: Houses and similar small residential buildings are generally exempt — read the application clauses
on.note: Hotels: 10% of suites, to a maximum of 20, need a barrier-free path of travel to the suite entrance (3.8.2.4).

TOPICS.title: Accessible entrances and power doors
TOPICS.summary: How many entrances must be accessible, and which doors need power operators.
TOPICS.tags: entrance principal entrance power door operator automatic door vestibule

values: New in 2024: power-operated doors at building entrances and at accessible washroom entrances in new commercial and public buildings
bc.note: Check 3.8.2.2 for how many pedestrian entrances must be accessible.

values: Number of barrier-free entrances from Table 3.8.1.2; one of them must be the principal entrance
Power door operator on doors through a barrier-free entrance in Group A, B (Divisions 2 and 3), C, D and E occupancies
Power door operator on the door from a vestibule into the floor area

TOPICS.title: Door clear width and hardware
TOPICS.summary: Doors on an accessible path need enough clear width, space beside the latch, and hardware within reach.
TOPICS.tags: door doorway clear width opening latch side hardware vision panel threshold

values: Clear opening ≥ 850 mm with the door open
Clear opening ≥ 850 mm with the door open at 90°
Clear space beside the latch: 600 mm when the door swings toward you, 300 mm when it swings away
Opening hardware 900–1100 mm above the floor
Vision panels at least 75 mm wide, bottom edge ≤ 900 mm above the floor

TOPICS.title: Accessible path of travel and turning space
TOPICS.summary: The route from the entrance to the spaces people use must be wide enough for a wheelchair, with room to turn.
TOPICS.tags: path of travel corridor width turning space circle wheelchair walk

values: Clear width ≥ 1000 mm
May narrow to 850 mm for a length of up to 600 mm
Turning space ≥ 1700 mm diameter, or the T-shaped alternative
bc.note: BCBC 2018 allowed a 920 mm path. Update older corridor and door details.

values: Exterior walks ≥ 1100 mm wide, slope ≤ 1 in 20
Headroom ≥ 1980 mm over the full width of a walk
Curb ramps ≥ 1500 mm wide, not counting the flared sides
Tactile attention indicators where required (3.8.3.18)
on.note: Check Subsection 3.8.3 for interior path of travel widths.

TOPICS.title: Ramps
TOPICS.summary: Slope, width, landings and handrails for ramps on an accessible path.
TOPICS.tags: ramp slope gradient landing handrail curb guard

values: Slope ≤ 1 in 12
Clear width ≥ 1000 mm
Landings at the top and bottom ≥ 1700 × 1700 mm
Intermediate landings at intervals ≤ 9 m
Handrails 865–965 mm high
Slope ≤ 1 in 12
≥ 900 mm between handrails
Landings at the top and bottom ≥ 1670 × 1670 mm
Intermediate landings at intervals ≤ 9 m
Handrails 865–965 mm high, extending ≥ 300 mm past the top and bottom
Guards ≥ 1070 mm high where required; curb ≥ 50 mm high at open edges

TOPICS.title: Universal washrooms and accessible stalls
TOPICS.summary: Where accessible washrooms are needed, and the clear spaces, fixtures and grab bars inside them.
TOPICS.tags: washroom toilet universal stall water closet grab bar lavatory sink mirror changing table

values: New in 2024: universal washrooms in new commercial and public buildings include a full-size adult changing space
Power-operated door at accessible washroom entrances
bc.note: Stall, water closet and grab bar dimensions changed with NBC 2020. Read Subsection 3.8.3 before reusing an older washroom layout.

values: Universal toilet room: open turning space ≥ 1700 mm diameter
Accessible stall: turning space ≥ 1500 mm diameter; door clear opening ≥ 860 mm
Water closet seat 430–485 mm above the floor; centerline 460–480 mm from the side wall
L-shaped side grab bar with 750 mm horizontal and vertical legs; rear grab bar ≥ 600 mm long
Lavatory rim ≤ 865 mm above the floor
Mirror with its bottom edge ≤ 1000 mm above the floor
Power door operator on a universal toilet room door that has a self-closer

TOPICS.title: Elevators and access between floors
TOPICS.summary: Which storeys must be reached by an accessible path, and when an elevator is required.
TOPICS.tags: elevator lift platform lift storey floor vertical access

values: New in 2024: an elevator is required in large two- and three-storey commercial and public buildings
bc.note: Check Subsection 3.8.2 for the size and occupancy thresholds.

on.note: Check Subsection 3.8.2 for which floor areas need a barrier-free path of travel.

TOPICS.title: Adaptable dwelling units
TOPICS.summary: Apartment units designed so they can be adapted later for people with disabilities.
TOPICS.tags: adaptable dwelling unit apartment condominium residential suite housing

values: In force from March 10, 2025
At least 1 in 5 units must be adaptable in large condominium and apartment buildings, and on the first floor of smaller ones
Not required for units over two storeys, units with their own entrance from outside, or units not reached by an interior accessible corridor

Includes accessible clearances through doors and along the path to the living space, clear space in a bedroom, bathroom and kitchen, controls at accessible heights, and bathroom walls reinforced for future grab bars
bc.note: The province publishes a free illustrated design guide (linked below).

on.note: Ontario has no adaptable dwelling unit rule like BC's Subsection 3.8.5.

TOPICS.title: Wheelchair spaces in assembly seating
TOPICS.summary: Theatres, lecture halls and other fixed-seat venues need designated wheelchair spaces.
TOPICS.tags: assembly seating theatre auditorium lecture hall wheelchair space

values: 2 to 99 fixed seats: at least 2 wheelchair spaces
Larger venues: more spaces, per the table

on.note: Check the Ontario table for the number of wheelchair spaces.

TOPICS.title: Accessible parking
TOPICS.summary: How many accessible parking stalls a building needs.
TOPICS.tags: parking stall accessible parking garage

values: 2–10 stalls: 1 accessible stall
11–25 stalls: 2 accessible stalls
More stalls: see the table
bc.note: Municipal zoning by-laws may ask for more.

on.note: Accessible parking in Ontario is set mainly by the AODA Design of Public Spaces standard (O. Reg. 191/11) and municipal by-laws, not the Building Code.

TOPICS.title: Controls and switches
TOPICS.summary: Switches, buttons and other controls on an accessible path must be within reach from a wheelchair.
TOPICS.tags: controls switch button outlet thermostat reach height

values: Operable controls 900–1200 mm above the floor

on.note: Check Subsection 3.8.3 for control and push-plate heights.

Bathroom: Clear space in front of toilet
